BATTERIES.name: Batteries & Power Cells
BATTERIES.description: Lithium-ion, Lead-acid, and Ni-Cd / Ni-MH rechargeable batteries harvested from electronics.
hazards: Thermal runaway and spontaneous fire risk if punctured or crushed
Corrosive sulfuric acid in lead-acid units
BATTERIES.handling_guidance: Tape battery terminals with non-conductive tape. Store in dry, insulated, fire-resistant drums. Never incinerate or drop from heights.

CABLES.name: Cables & Wiring Harnesses
CABLES.description: Insulated copper wiring, aluminum conductors, power supply cords, and data cables.
sub_types: USB, HDMI, Ethernet, & Data Patch Cords
hazards: Dioxin and furan emission if open-burned (Strictly illegal under E-Waste Rules!)
Lead and phthalate plasticizers in PVC insulation
CABLES.handling_guidance: Do NOT burn cables to extract copper. Authorized recyclers use mechanical wire strippers and granulators with pneumatic air-density separators.

CRT.name: Cathode Ray Tubes (CRT TVs & Monitors)
CRT.description: Bulky legacy glass picture tubes from old cathode-ray televisions, computer monitors, and oscilloscopes.
hazards: High vacuum implosion hazard during dismantling
Extremely high lead content (up to 2-3 kg of Lead oxide in funnel glass)
Toxic luminescent phosphor coating (Cadmium, Zinc sulfide)
CRT.handling_guidance: Keep vacuum tube intact; discharge anode voltage (>25kV capacitor store) before handling. Wear safety goggles. Do NOT smash or discard glass in municipal dumps.

LCD_LED.name: Flat Display Panels (LCD, LED, OLED)
LCD_LED.description: Flat screen displays from LED/LCD televisions, computer monitors, laptops, and tablets.
hazards: Mercury vapor in older Cold Cathode Fluorescent Lamp (CCFL) backlights
Liquid crystal compounds (potential persistent organic pollutants)
LCD_LED.handling_guidance: Stack horizontally on padded pallets. Prevent panel twisting or cracking to prevent mercury gas release from CCFL tubes.

PCB.name: Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs)
PCB.description: Motherboards, logic boards, circuit cards, and populated PCBs from all electronics.
sub_types: High-Grade: Smartphone, Laptop, & Server Motherboards (High Gold/Palladium)
Medium-Grade: Telecom, Network Router, Sound/Video Cards, RAM/Memory
Low-Grade: Brown/Yellow Phenolic TV, Radio, & Power Supply Boards
hazards: Brominated Flame Retardants (BFRs) in epoxy resins
PCB.handling_guidance: Keep intact without destructive acid baths or open flame desoldering. Store in waterproof crates to prevent copper and metal leaching.

MOTORS_MAGNETS.name: Motors, Transformers, & Neodymium Magnets
MOTORS_MAGNETS.description: Electromechanical actuators, compressors, step motors, ferrite/rare-earth magnets, and heavy transformers.
sub_types: AC/DC Induction Motors (Washing machines, fans, blenders)
Hard Disk Drive Voice-Coil Neodymium Magnets (NdFeB)
hazards: Extremely powerful pinch hazard from high-grade rare-earth magnets
MOTORS_MAGNETS.handling_guidance: Keep strong neodymium magnets away from mechanical watches, credit cards, and cardiac pacemakers.

MIXED_PLASTICS.name: Engineering E-Plastics (ABS, HIPS, PC)
MIXED_PLASTICS.description: Rigid structural plastic shells and casings from electronic appliances and computers.
hazards: Brominated flame retardants (OctaBDE, DecaBDE) requiring spectroscopic separation under RoHS
MIXED_PLASTICS.handling_guidance: Remove metal inserts, screws, and rubber feet before baling. Keep dry and segregated by polymer code if marked.

MIXED_OTHER.name: Mixed & Unsorted E-Waste Scrap
MIXED_OTHER.description: Composite electronic waste assemblies, unsorted gadget lots, and combined electronic hardware.
valuable_materials: Combined base and precious metal recovery
hazards: Variable composite hazards; mixed battery leakage risk
MIXED_OTHER.handling_guidance: Inspect for damaged lithium batteries before compaction. Transport in heavy duty bulk bags.

examples: Used blood glucose meters with lancets
ICU patient monitoring lines with bodily fluids
prohibited_and_rejected_items.rejection_reason: Severe biohazard and pathogen transmission risk. Regulated strictly under Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016. E-waste recyclers are NOT legally authorized to process medical bio-waste.
prohibited_and_rejected_items.disposal_route: Color-coded biohazard yellow/red bins to Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facility (CBWTF).

prohibited_and_rejected_items.rejection_reason: Contains ionizing radionuclide isotopes. Regulated exclusively by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB). Severe criminal penalties for unauthorized scrap trading.
prohibited_and_rejected_items.disposal_route: Report to AERB or return to authorized nuclear material disposal agency.

examples: Undissipated high-capacity capacitors in industrial switchgear
prohibited_and_rejected_items.rejection_reason: Catastrophic explosion and toxic gas inhalation risk during baling or shredding.
prohibited_and_rejected_items.disposal_route: Degassing and evacuation by certified HVAC recovery technicians prior to scrap acceptance.

prohibited_and_rejected_items.rejection_reason: Non-electronic biodegradable matter. Contaminates electronic scrap sorting machinery and causes rot.
prohibited_and_rejected_items.disposal_route: Municipal organic waste composting or wet waste processing facility.

prohibited_and_rejected_items.rejection_reason: Non-engineering consumer commodity packaging plastic. Handled by dry waste plastic aggregators, NOT e-waste recyclers under EPR E-Waste Rules.
prohibited_and_rejected_items.disposal_route: Deposit at local dry waste collection centers (DWCC) or with general plastic kabadiwalas.
